findings.what: test_glyph_preset_in_dither_context_keeps_its_registered_renderer pins the opposite of the literal accept item for the default call. With no available=, a glyph preset in a dither context returns glyph_ramp with no warning.
findings.why: The accept item says a glyph preset in a dither context returns a warning and a pixel renderer. That only holds when the host passes available={'pixel'}. This follows from §6 (fallback only when the renderer is absent) and the human arbitrage, but it is a documented soft spot.
findings.fix: Make sure the dither host wires available= to its own renderer set. Record the decision in DEVIATIONS.md so the accept item is not read as unconditional.

findings.what: Several tests need glyph_ramp and braille to be registered. test_registered_non_table_renderer_is_kept asserts on braille. Every glyph fixture load asserts warnings == [].
findings.why: These tests couple L4 to renderers owned by other cards. They pass in orchestrator isolation but would fail on a base without those renderers.
findings.fix: Pass available= explicitly in these tests, or monkeypatch the registry.

findings.what: APP_DEFAULT_RENDERER hardcodes the application names "glyph" and "glitch" inside lattice_core.
findings.why: This is data, not an import, so it is not a hard E8 leak. The only test is the AST import check, which cannot see it.
findings.fix: Optionally let apps register their default renderer. Otherwise document the table as an accepted exception.

findings.what: Legacy v1/v2 loads drop colliding v3 keys (pipeline, app, effects) from extra.
findings.why: This is documented and tested, but it is a narrow exception to the "unknown keys preserved" rule.

notes: I checked this by reading the diff only and did not run the tests. Every accept item has a test. The fixtures and the version, seed, section and effect-entry error handling are covered. Continuous-mode nulls round-trip through JSON and PipelineSpec. There are no application imports and no host coupling. The attempt-4 test (available={'pixel'}) is the accept-item test that was missing.
